Saturn last moved through Capricorn from {{previousResidencyEntryDateWithYear}} to {{previousResidencyExitDateWithYear}}. By the end of that transit, the pandemic had made hidden work impossible to ignore. entries.ownerVerbatimWithDates: Saturn takes about 29 years to move through all twelve signs, spending around two and a half years in each. Saturn last moved through Capricorn from December 20, 2017 to December 17, 2020. By the end of that transit, the pandemic had made hidden work impossible to ignore. Hospitals, schools, households, and workplaces all discovered how quickly a system can strain when the people carrying its invisible work are pushed past what their staffing, hours, bodies, and resources can sustain.

entries.body: Earlier Saturn-in-Capricorn periods also arrived during years when major systems were being dismantled, reinforced, or rebuilt. From 1929 to 1933, financial collapse exposed weaknesses in banks and markets and forced a new argument over how much responsibility government should carry for economic stability. From 1959 to 1962, colonial rule was breaking apart across Africa while the Cold War hardened into new borders and confrontations, including the Berlin Wall. From 1989 to 1992, the Berlin Wall fell, Germany reunified, the Soviet Union dissolved, and the Maastricht Treaty began building a new political structure for Europe. The events are different, and the same disorientation runs through all of them: a structure everyone had organized their lives around stopped being permanent. The recurring question begins once everyone can see that the old structure no longer holds: what gets rebuilt, who takes responsibility for it, and what is no longer worth preserving?
